description: Hosmer-Lemeshow Calibration Test Suite Self-contained tests for the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic, used to assess calibration of logistic regression models.
comments: Hosmer-Lemeshow Calibration Test Suite
Self-contained tests for the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic,
used to assess calibration of logistic regression models.
The HL statistic partitions predictions into 10 decile bins and computes
a chi-squared statistic comparing observed vs. expected event counts.
Under good calibration HL ~ χ²(8) (8 df since outer cells are constrained).
Reference: Hosmer & Lemeshow, "Goodness-of-fit tests for the multiple
logistic regression model", Comm. Stat. Theory Methods (1980).
All functions inlined (tests cannot import stdlib).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `reinhart_rogoff`. Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
comments: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo
The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with
debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
in the EU, US, and UK.
Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) found three compounding errors:
1. UNIT ERROR:    growth stored as percentage points but treated as fractions
2. SAMPLE ERROR:  Excel formula excluded 5 high-debt, high-growth countries
3. UNCERTAINTY:   4 country-observations — result was within noise floor
Corrected result: +2.2% growth (not -0.1%). The threshold claim was noise.
This demo shows all three errors in Sounio's epistemic tracking:
- Units: explicit fraction/pp conversion — confusion is visible
- Provenance: excluded sample is a missing branch in the computation graph
- Uncertainty: SNR < 1 makes the "threshold effect" formally indefensible
Data sources: Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) Table 3; HAP Working Paper 322.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `test_fem`. - Tests for the finite element method module Self-contained test suite for 1D bar elements, 2D CST triangles, constitutive matrices, assembly, solvers (direct + CG), boundary. It should compile and run successfully.
description: - Tests for the finite element method module Self-contained test suite for 1D bar elements, 2D CST triangles, constitutive matrices, assembly, solvers (direct + CG), boundary
comments: test_fem.sio -- Tests for the finite element method module
Self-contained test suite for 1D bar elements, 2D CST triangles,
constitutive matrices, assembly, solvers (direct + CG), boundary
conditions, and mesh generation. All helpers copied from stdlib/math/fem.sio.
Tests:
1.  1D stiffness matrix symmetry: ke[0][1] = ke[1][0]
2.  1D stiffness trace: ke[0][0] + ke[1][1] = 2*EA/L
3.  1D mass matrix positive entries
4.  Triangle area: known triangle with area = 0.5
5.  Triangle shape functions sum to 1 at any point
6.  Triangle shape functions at vertices: N_i(vertex_j) = delta_ij
7.  Plane stress matrix symmetry: D[0][1] = D[1][0]
8.  1D bar exact solution: fixed-free bar, distributed load
9.  2D patch test: uniform stress state recovered by CST elements
10.  CG solver matches direct solver for same system
11.  Dirichlet penalty BC: K[dof][dof] >> other entries
12.  Mesh generation: 1D uniform mesh has correct node/element count
